title: Bugfix: EvidencePool re-adds a previous_result row every time a task result changes (10,676 rows, 1.8 MB for goal T-0991); key previous_result by task id and keep the latest, skip superseded tasks
spec: Observed real 21:55: .orchestrator/evidence/T-0991.jsonl held 10,676 previous_result rows (1.8 MB of content) for about 280 tasks because EvidencePool.add dedupes by content hash and a task result changes content on every status update; the legacy evidence section then rendered 2.26 MB into a review packet (argv too long, review T-1279 post_failed) and active routing spent its budget on stale result rows. Fix in orchestrator/evidence.py: previous_result evidence is keyed by (source_type, location) and add() replaces the existing row for that key when the content differs instead of appending (write the file back or mark the old row superseded on load, whichever the existing persistence supports without a rewrite on every add; a compaction on load that keeps only the latest row per key is acceptable); rows whose task is superseded on the bus are dropped at load. Also cap the legacy evidence section in spawn._packet_body at [context_router].legacy_evidence_chars (default 6000, dated comment) so a shadow or off router can never build an unbounded packet. Regression tests in tests/test_evidence.py and tests/test_spawn.py. Repository rules: unittest, no new dependencies, run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green, do not ask questions.
acceptance: tests/test_evidence.py::test_previous_result_rows_replace_by_location_and_skip_superseded (adding three versions of one task result keeps one row; a superseded task row is dropped on load)
